title: 1 Hr Axe Throwing Session
description: Singapore's first axe throwing range lets you channel your inner Viking for a solid hour. Great for blowing off steam, celebrating birthdays, or just doing something wildly different on a weekend. An experienced instructor guides you through proper technique, and yes — there's even a birthday cake-cutting axe moment. 🪓

host.name: The Axe Factor
host.bio:
Axe Factor Sentosa offers a unique and thrilling experience for both tourists and locals looking to spice up their leisure time. Nestled in the vibrant heart of Sentosa Island, Singapore, this premier axe throwing venue provides an adventurous escape where participants can unleash their inner warrior.

Ideal for friends, family, or corporate groups, Axe Factor offers a blend of fun, challenge, and excitement. Whether you're a seasoned axe thrower or a beginner eager to learn, the expert coaches ensure a safe and enjoyable experience. After throwing axes, visitors can explore the island's numerous attractions, making it a perfect day out.

Embrace the thrill of axe throwing at Axe Factor Sentosa – where fun meets adrenaline in Singapore's most iconic leisure destination! 

Important Note: Each booking timeslot allows a maximum of 5 pax.

title: 3-Hour Adults Watercolour Painting Workshop – Singapore Themed / Floral
description: Pick your vibe — paint iconic Singapore landmarks like shophouses and Raffles Hotel, or go floral with sunflowers and peonies. Professional artist Kanchan Mehendale guides you through watercolour basics, layering, and blending over 3 relaxed hours. All materials provided, sketch prepped for you, and zero judgment on the finished product — just good vibes and a painting to bring home.

title: 3 hr Embroidery Workshop (Age 7+)
description: Pick up embroidery from scratch in this 3-hour hands-on workshop at Sage Artelier Studio in Sin Ming. No arts background needed — experienced instructors guide you through every stitch. You'll bring home your own finished piece, plus all materials are provided. Great for families, dates, or just a chill creative afternoon.

title: Adult Personalised Art Lessons
description: Pick up painting or drawing at your own pace in a relaxed open-studio setting. Choose your medium — acrylics, watercolour, oil, charcoal, you name it — and work on whatever you want with guidance from a teaching artist. Great for total beginners and rusty creatives alike. All materials included, no judgment vibes only.

title: Aerial Yoga (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced)
description: Hang upside down in a silk hammock and finally understand what "decompressing" actually means. Sky Yoga's aerial yoga classes blend traditional yoga, Pilates, and a dash of acrobatics — good for your back, your flexibility, and your Instagram. Suitable for total beginners to seasoned yogis, with levels to match.

title: Aerial Yoga Class
description: Ever wanted to try yoga but with a hammock doing half the work? Dream Dance and Yoga's Aerial Yoga class is open to all levels — no flexibility required. You'll build core strength, improve posture, and get a solid stretch in spots regular yoga can't reach. Bonus: that floaty, weightless feeling is genuinely hard to beat.

title: Aerial Yoga in Singapore
description: Ditch the mat and take your practice into the air — Yoga Sadhana's Aerial Yoga classes use silk hammocks to help you stretch deeper, build core strength, and nail those inversions you've been scared of. Good for total beginners and experienced yogis alike, with certified instructors keeping things safe and fun. Small class sizes mean you actually get attention, not just vibes.

title: Amazing Race SG
description: A city-wide scavenger hunt across Singapore's neighbourhoods. Clues, checkpoints, and a fair amount of arguing about which MRT line to take. Good luck!

host.name: The Rally Co. Team
host.bio: Rally Co. has been running city-wide adventure experiences across Singapore since 2015. Their facilitators are ex-event producers and avid urban explorers who know every shortcut, hawker stall, and hidden corner of the island.

whatToExpect:
Your team will be split into groups of 5–8 and handed a sealed envelope at the starting point. Inside: your first clue.

Over 3.5 hours you'll navigate across 6–8 checkpoints spread across Singapore's neighbourhoods — on foot, MRT, and the occasional taxi scramble. Each checkpoint has a challenge: a trivia question, a physical task, or a local vendor you need to track down.

The winning team gets bragging rights and a group photo at the finish line. Every team gets a debrief with the funniest moments from the day.

title: Art Master Series – Watercolour Landscape Painting Workshop with Ong Kim Seng
description: Paint alongside celebrated Singaporean watercolourist Ong Kim Seng in this outdoor plein air session at Chinatown. You'll start with 45 mins of sketching, then dive into watercolour techniques on-site and back at the studio. Great for beginners and experienced painters alike — all materials included, and you get to bring your masterpiece home.

title: Art of Photography Workshop
description: Step out of the classroom and into the streets with Leica's guided outdoor photography workshop. Led by instructor KC Eng, you'll practise exposure, composition, and zoom techniques on real subjects — not just slides. Bring any camera you own; Leica gear is available to borrow too. Good for beginners who already know their aperture from their ISO.
location: City Hall / Beach Road (South Beach Quarter)

title: Axe Factor – 1 Hr Axe Throwing
description: Ever wanted to hurl an axe at something without getting in trouble? Axe Factor on Sentosa lets you do exactly that. Expert coaches guide you through the whole thing, so even total beginners can get the hang of it pretty fast. Great for a group hangout, date, or just a random Tuesday that needs more excitement.

title: Axe Throwing Experience in Singapore
description: Ever wanted to hurl an axe at something and call it a sport? Axe Factor lets you do exactly that. You get 60 mins of unlimited throws, a proper safety briefing, and a coach to help you nail that bullseye. Go solo or bring your kakis — there's even a round-robin tournament to settle who's the real lumberjack among you.

title: Axe Throwing Experience
description: Singapore's first and only axe throwing facility, tucked in Sentosa's Mess Hall. Coach-guided sessions mean total beginners are welcome — they'll walk you through technique and safety before you start hurling. Pick your game mode, bring your kakis, and yes, you can upgrade to a tomahawk.

title: Bartending & Mixology Workshop
description: Learn to shake, muddle, and stir like a pro with The Shake Affinity's mixologists. Go from bartending basics all the way to advanced cocktail-making — then drink what you made. Can be set up at your office, home, hotel, or pretty much anywhere in Singapore. Great for team-building or just a solid excuse to learn cocktails.

title: Basic 3-Item Workshop (Italian Buttero Museum Leather)
description: Learn the basics of leatherworking with full-grain Italian vegetable-tanned leather from Tuscany. You'll craft a cardholder, luggage tag, and key fob — all in one session — and personalise them with hot foil stamping. No experience needed, and you walk out with three proper handmade pieces the same day.

title: Basic Fine Script Calligraphy Workshop
description: Learn the art of dip pen calligraphy in this 3-hour hands-on workshop led by Joanne from The Letter J Supply. You'll go from zero to writing connected script by the end — basic strokes, minuscules, and letter connections all covered. No prior experience needed, and all materials (pen holder, nibs, ink, booklet) are yours to take home.

title: Bean to Bar Chocolate-making Workshop
description: Singapore's only live bean-to-bar chocolate workshop where you actually roast raw cacao beans and mould your own chocolate bar in one session. You'll also get to explore their green sanctuary with real cacao trees and bees. Held every Saturday afternoon — great for food nerds and chocolate lovers who want more than just eating the thing.

title: Kintsugi Art Studio
description:
Kintsugi is Japan's ancient art of celebrating broken pottery. It is rooted in an eastern philosophy of finding beauty in imperfections. Many believe it can help us to accept our flaws and foster a sense of peace and fulfillment.

https://www.kintsugiartstudio.com/

host.name: The Kintsugi Team
host.bio: The Kintsugi Art Studio team are passionate practitioners of the Japanese art form, trained in both the traditional urushi lacquer technique and modern adaptations. They believe the practice of repair is as meaningful as the object itself.

whatToExpect:
You'll begin by selecting a piece of broken pottery — or bringing your own — and understanding the philosophy behind kintsugi: that breakage and repair are part of an object's history, not something to hide.

Using a food-safe, non-toxic lacquer mixed with gold powder, you'll carefully fill each crack with deliberate brushwork. The process is meditative and unhurried.

Your piece will need 24–48 hours to cure fully. The studio will wrap it carefully for transport. You'll leave with both the repaired piece and a deeper appreciation for imperfection.

title: Bread Foundation Class for Beginners
description: Learn to bake soft, fluffy Asian-style bread from scratch — think coffee buns, scallion buns, and sandwich loaves. A hands-on 5-hour session in a boutique studio with max 8 students, so you actually get proper guidance. Everything's provided, and you bring home a full bag of bakes. No pork, no lard, halal-friendly.

title: BreathEra® Breathwork Class
description: Not your typical "just breathe deeply" class — BreathEra® is a neuroscience-backed breathwork programme that trains your nervous system to actually handle stress better. Expect diaphragmatic drills, breath-holds, and rhythm work that target your parasympathetic system. Good for burned-out folks, poor sleepers, or anyone whose body's been running on fumes. Trial sessions are open for booking.

title: Breathwork Circle
description: A guided breathwork session that helps regulate your nervous system and ease the weight of daily stress. Led by trained facilitators, this Facilitated Breath Repatterning circle is a proper slow-down — no yoga mat gymnastics, just you and your breath. Good for when life's been a lot lately.

title: Candle Making Workshop
description: Learn to make your own scented candles from scratch — including gel candles with that cool see-through look. Great for a chill afternoon or a team bonding session that's actually fun. SGArtClass guides you through everything, so no experience needed. Walk away with something you actually made (and it smells good too).

title: Candle Making Workshop Singapore
description: Pick your candle type — gel or soy — and spend 1.5 hours learning to mix fragrances, pick colours, and pour wax into your own custom container. Great for beginners and big groups alike. Held at their air-conditioned studio near Mattar MRT, or they can come to you. Walk away with something that actually smells good.

title: Candle Making Workshop Singapore
description: Pick your wax, pick your scent, go home with a candle you actually made yourself. FunEmpire runs gel and soy candle-making sessions good for corporate groups or just a chill hangout. Starts from $32/pax, island-wide locations or they'll come to you. Low pressure, beginner-friendly, and you keep what you make.

title: Candle Making Workshop
description: Pick your scent, pour your wax, and walk away with a candle you actually made yourself. FunEmpire's candle workshop is chill, beginner-friendly, and works for everything from team bonding to birthday hangs. Choose between gel or soy candles — all materials provided, no experience needed. Studio's in Tai Seng but they can come to you too.

title: One-of-a-kind pottery in Tiong Bahru | Lush Garden, Kid-friendly (4+)
description:
This hidden gem is a whole new pottery experience. Nestled in a lush, leafy garden in Tiong Bahru, you'll spend a blissful few hours getting your hands delightfully muddy under the expert eye of a true creative designer. Forget run-of-the-mill bowls and mugs – think quirky sloth cups, or plates adorned with your gorgeous fur babies. This is hand-building pottery with an extra dose of personality!



What to expect

Leave everyday stress at the garden gate – this is your creative oasis.
Learn the ancient art of hand-building pottery – no intimidating wheels here!
Let your imagination run wild – your host will guide you to bring those unique piece ideas to life.
Celebrate a special occasion? You can customize your ceramic creation for birthdays, proposals...the sky's the limit!
Kiddos in tow? They'll love this pottery adventure where they create and paint their piece in one fun session.


Important tips

This cozy experience needs at least 2 people to run. Perfect for a creative date or gathering a small group of friends!
Your one-of-a-kind masterpieces will need 3-4 weeks for glazing and firing before you take them home.

host.name: Emily Lim
host.bio: Emily's backyard pottery studio is a hidden gem! A former creative designer, she's got a knack for turning your wildest ideas into beautiful ceramic pieces. Emily's warm, patient style and years of experience make her the perfect guide on your pottery journey.

whatToExpect:
You'll arrive to a studio that smells unreasonably good. After a short intro on wax types and fragrance blending, you'll choose your scent combination from over 30 options and pick your vessel — from classic tins to ceramic pots.

The pouring process takes about 45 minutes. While your candle sets, Sarah walks you through care tips: why cotton wicks matter, how to get a clean burn, and how to re-use the vessel once the wax is gone.

You'll leave with one completed candle (plus any extras you make if time allows). No experience needed — if you can pour a cup of coffee, you can make a candle.

title: Certificate in Oil Painting (Basic)
description: Learn oil painting from scratch at NAFA's Centre for Lifelong Education. Over 12 sessions, you'll get hands-on with colour mixing, brushwork, and composition — and walk away with a proper still life portfolio. Great for total beginners who want a structured, legit foundation rather than a one-off dabble.

title: Chocolate Bar Workshop @ 2am:dessertbar
description: Get hands-on making your own chocolate bar at Janice Wong's iconic 2am:dessertbar. Great for chocolate lovers who want more than just eating — you actually make something. Casual, creative, and pretty satisfying for a weeknight out.

title: Chocolate Making with Embrace Chocolate (Halal)
description: Ever wanted to make your own chocolate from scratch? Learn how to melt and temper chocolate, then go wild designing your own chocolate bark with nuts, dried fruit, spices and more. End the session with a hot chocolate you made yourself, plus a 3-course plant-based meal. Halal-friendly and great for curious foodies.

title: Chocolate Truffles Making Workshop
description: Make your own dark chocolate truffles from scratch with a pro chocolatier guiding you through it. While your truffles set, you'll also customise your own chocolate bar. Go home with 12–15 truffles and a bar — not bad for two hours' work. Great for groups, team bonding, or just an excuse to eat a lot of chocolate.

title: Closed Terrarium (Moss Terrarium) Workshop
description: Get your hands dirty (literally) building your own closed moss terrarium from scratch — layering lecca, soil, live moss, and plants into a self-sustaining little ecosystem. No experience needed; the Green Chapter folks walk you through every step. Takes about an hour, and you leave with something actually worth putting on your shelf.

title: Cocktail Masterclass & DIY Session!
description: Learn the art of cocktail-making from a pro bartender — think history, techniques, and a hands-on DIY session where you taste everything you make. Break into teams, compete for the "Best Original Cocktail" title, and go home with recipes to show off. Great for a fun night out, date night, or team bonding. Mocktail options available too.

title: Cocktail Mixology Class in Singapore
description: Ever wanted to make that perfect Negroni or Whisky Sour yourself? This hands-on mixology class teaches you the real basics — shaking, stirring, muddling, and balancing flavours like a proper bartender. You'll craft classics like Mojitos and Daiquiris, plus mocktail options too. Great for date nights, team bonding, or just a fun Friday that isn't another bar tab.

title: Cultural Cooking Class Singapore
description: Learn to cook proper Singaporean dishes — think Laksa, Curry Chicken, Nasi Lemak — using real family recipes passed down through generations. Run by a social enterprise with genuinely warm instructors, this 3-hour hands-on class covers local food culture stories before you sit down to eat what you made. No cooking experience needed, and yes, the food actually tastes good.

title: Embroidery Workshop
description: Learn the basics of hand embroidery and stitch your own design onto a cup holder or pouch — no experience needed. Craft Labs keeps groups small so trainers can give proper guidance. Great for a chill weekend activity, team bonding, or even a hens party. All materials provided, just bring your hands.

title: E.S.C. - Escape @ Science Centre
description: Not your typical escape room with combination locks — E.S.C. mixes STEM puzzles, theatrical storylines, and wild physical elements like ball-filled enclosures and shaking floors. Pick from three worlds: Museum of Humankind, Shangri-La, or Dr. X. Great for groups who want something more hands-on and legit challenging. One room even lets you use your phone, so your IG is safe.

title: Singapore Wake Park
description:
The Park features two straight-line systems. System A (60 meters) is designed for complete beginners, offering wakeboarding lessons led by our experienced instructors.

The system runs one rider at a time, providing a safe, focused learning environment with full instructor attention. Its gradual cable speed makes learning the basics easier, making it ideal for young children.

The Park runs 9 lessons daily, each lasting 1 hour, with a maximum of 4 riders per lesson.

Rate:
$55 per rider/hour or 1 hour off Share-The-Fun Pass
Includes: Helmet, Vest & House Wakeboard (Non-Obstacle)
Obstacle Wakeboard Rental: $20/Session

- Rate is inclusive of GST & applicable daily
- Recommended age for a participating child is 6 years old & above
- All riders are required to know basic swimming

host.name: Wakeboard Singapore
host.bio: The Locked SG team are puzzle designers, ex-corporate trainers, and enthusiastic chaos-causers. They've run over 500 team sessions and know exactly which moments reveal who your team really is under pressure.

whatToExpect:
Your group will be briefed on the scenario — typically a 60-minute escape challenge designed for 6–12 people simultaneously. Unlike solo escape rooms, this one is built for collaboration: clues are distributed across the team from the start.

After the room, a trained facilitator runs a 30-minute structured debrief. It's not a post-mortem — it's a genuine conversation about communication styles, decision-making under pressure, and what your team learned about itself.

No escape room experience needed. First-timers often have the most interesting debrief moments.

title: Floral Embroidery (Level 1)
description: Learn 10–15 embroidery techniques through floral and botanical patterns — no sewing experience needed. Over 4 sessions, you'll stitch designs onto a canvas bag you get to bring home. Taught by Cheryl, a Peranakan-inspired textile artist with 10+ years in design. A genuinely chill way to slow down and make something with your hands.

title: Floral Watercolour Workshop
description: Pick up watercolour painting the chill way — LACA's 2-hour floral workshop teaches you botanical illustration techniques developed by their founder. No experience needed, and you'll leave with an actual painting on proper cold-pressed paper. Over 1,000 students have gone through this, so you're in good hands.

title: Free Motion Embroidery Workshop
description: Ever wanted to ditch the straight line and actually have fun with your sewing machine? This intro workshop teaches you free motion embroidery — think drawing with thread. You'll learn basic FME techniques and go home with your very own embroidered tea towel. Must know how to use a sewing machine; open to ages 12 and up.

title: Fundamental Studio Lighting Course
description: Want to stop relying on natural light and actually control what you're shooting with? Mount Studio's foundational studio lighting course covers everything from light theory to hands-on strobe and modifier practice. Small class sizes (max 5) mean you actually get proper guidance, not just watch someone else shoot. Good for working photographers ready to level up their client offerings.

title: Fundamentals of Photography Workshop
description: New to photography or just tired of shooting on Auto? This 2-hour workshop at Leica's South Beach Quarter store covers the essentials — exposure triangle, composition, white balance, and more. No experience needed, and you don't have to own a Leica to join. A solid starting point if you actually want to understand your camera.

title: Golden Dragon Macramé Workshop
description: Looks like this page got blocked by Cloudflare before we could grab the details. Not enough info to tell you what this macramé workshop is really about — check back later or head to the source URL directly.

title: Guided Breathwork Sessions
description: Learn to hack your own nervous system through guided breathwork — covering methods like Wim Hof, Oxygen Advantage, and Holotropic Breathwork. Good for stressed-out professionals, athletes, or anyone who just needs to decompress properly. Sessions end with optional cold plunge and integration dialogue so you actually leave with usable tools.

title: Hand Embroidery on Clothes Workshop by Moshoo x FMS
description: A 2-session workshop where you'll learn hand embroidery techniques and actually put them to use on your own clothes. First session covers the basics with a practice sampler, then you bring in a piece of clothing to personalise in session two. Great for beginners who want a new way to refresh their wardrobe without spending on new stuff.

title: Hands-on Bread Making Workshops in Singapore
description: Five bread-making classes in one place — from Korean Garlic Cream Cheese Buns to proper Italian focaccia and ciabatta. Sessions run 3 to 6 hours depending on the class, and you get to eat what you bake. Great whether you've never touched dough or just want to level up your home baking game.

title: Hands-on Chocolate Techniques Workshop
description: Ever wanted to make your own truffles, pralines, or chocolate bars from scratch? This hands-on workshop covers everything from tempering and moulding to flavouring and presentation. You'll learn under professional chefs and walk away with actual chocolates you made yourself. Great for beginners and chocoholics who want something more than just eating the stuff.

title: Hands-on Japanese Ramen Cooking Class
description: Learn to make proper Japanese ramen from scratch — not the instant kind. You'll whip up Shoyu Ramen, Japanese Char Siew, Cabbage Rolls, and Namasu pickles, guided by an expert chef from prep to plating. Great for impressing friends or just levelling up your home cooking game.

title: One Day Scuba Singapore
description:
🇸🇬 Singapore-Based Open Water Course‍  ‍

Train and certify entirely in Singapore - perfect for tight schedules or local convenience.

host.name: Scuba Singapore
host.bio: Team Kopi are Singapore-born food educators who've spent years documenting hawker recipes before they disappear. They run the cook-off as a love letter to hawker culture — competitive, loud, and delicious.

whatToExpect:
Trying scuba for the first time can feel intimidating — but you're not alone. We’ve helped thousands of first-time divers become confident and certified.

Here’s why beginners choose us:

✅ Friendly, certified instructors who know how to coach first-timers  

✅ Step-by-step training, starting in a shallow pool  

✅ All dive equipment provided — just bring swimwear and curiosity  

✅ Choose between local or tropical open water locations

We’ll support you every step of the way, from your first breath underwater to your final qualifying dive.

title: Hawker Delights Cooking Class
description: Learn to whip up Singapore's most beloved hawker dishes — think chili crab, laksa, nasi lemak, and chicken rice — in a hands-on cooking class that's beginner-friendly. SkillsFuture credits applicable, so you can offset a big chunk of the $784.80 full fee. Max 24 pax, two to a cooking station, and yes, they provide all the ingredients and takeaway containers.

title: Historical Singapore Bicycle Tour by Let's Go Tour
description: Cycle ~20km through Singapore's iconic neighbourhoods — Chinatown, Kampong Glam, the Singapore River, and more — with a knowledgeable local guide. You'll get a proper peek at everyday Singapore life, hit up a market, and even sample some local food. Tours run rain or shine, so no excuses.

title: Historical Singapore Bicycle Tour
description: Hop on a bike and spend 4 hours cycling through Singapore's most iconic neighbourhoods — Kampong Gelam, Chinatown, the CBD, Marina Bay, and even a stretch of the F1 circuit. Your guide keeps it real with a pit stop at a local kopitiam for a snack and drink. Runs daily, rain or shine (minus thunderstorms).

title: Holotropic Breathwork Workshop
description: Go deep — like, really deep. This 6-hour breathwork workshop uses rhythmic breathing and music to guide you into altered states of consciousness for emotional release and self-discovery. Led by Punam Rai, Singapore's only GTT-certified Holotropic Breathwork facilitator. Includes two breathing rounds, mandala drawing, and a group integration circle. Not your average chill session.

title: How To: Advanced Silkscreen Printing Workshop (Drawn to Silkscreen)
description: Ever wanted to see your own doodle on a tote bag? How To Ink walks you through the full silkscreen process — from drawing your design to printing it using real UV emulsion technique. Expect some troubleshooting along the way (that's part of the fun). Max 5 pax, by appointment only.

title: HyperDrive: Electric Indoor Go-Karting Experience
description: Singapore's first multi-level indoor electric go-kart track — 308 metres, 14 turns, and legit gamified racing elements. Whether you're a total beginner or a speed demon with a licence, there's a kart for you. Air-conditioned, so no excuses about the weather. Great for families or a competitive hangout with friends.

title: Improv for Workplaces
description: No scripts, no presentations — just your team learning to listen, adapt, and say yes to each other. Improv exercises that translate directly into better collaboration.

host.name: The Yes And SG Collective
host.bio: Yes And SG is Singapore's longest-running workplace improv company, founded by actors, coaches, and one former management consultant who got tired of PowerPoint. Their facilitators have worked with teams from MNCs to scrappy startups.

whatToExpect:
The session opens with low-stakes warm-up games — think word-association and mirroring exercises — designed to get people out of their heads and into the room.

From there, the facilitators introduce the core improv principle: 'Yes, and.' Every scene builds on what the other person says, rather than blocking or redirecting. You'll do this in pairs, then small groups, then as a full team.

The last hour involves longer-form exercises that map directly onto real work scenarios: handling unexpected feedback, staying present in a chaotic meeting, listening without preparing your reply. No performance experience needed — some of the best sessions involve people who said they'd be terrible at this.

title: IPPUDO Child Kitchen Ramen And Gyoza Making Workshop
description: Make ramen from scratch — like, actually stomp on the dough with your feet. IPPUDO's Child Kitchen workshop walks you through kneading dough, crafting gyoza skins, and rolling out noodles before sitting down to eat what you made. Great for families or adults who just really love Japanese food. Sessions are limited and book up fast, so sign up for their mailing list.

title: Journaling with Nature
description: Combine mindful journaling with hands-on plant care in this two-format programme led by mental health advocate Mahita Vas. Choose a 1-hour drop-in session to journal and pot a succulent, or go deeper with a 3-hour workshop where you'll write, reflect, and build your own terrarium. Great for anyone who needs a proper pause from the daily grind.

title: Journey To The Art Of Mixology Cocktail Masterclass
description: Ever wanted to actually know what you're doing behind a bar? Learn to craft your own bespoke cocktails under the guidance of the folks at award-winning Maison Ikkoku. Pick your style — classic or extra Insta-worthy — and walk away with real skills (and a full stomach, canapes included). 18+ only, lah.

title: Kayak & Canoe Rental
description: Grab a kayak or canoe and paddle around the Kallang Basin — no booking needed, just walk in. Great for families, beginners, and anyone who wants to be on the water without too much planning. Keep an eye out for the resident otters while you're at it. Rentals come in 2-hour or full-day options.

title: KF1 Kiddy Circuit
description: Singapore's first immersive go-karting experience built for kids — think real go-karts, radio-controlled cars, and VR driving all under one roof. There's even a 30-metre interactive projection wall to make each race feel extra dramatic. Safe, child-friendly, and genuinely fun for parents to watch too. Located at Singapore Expo Hall 8A.

title: Kids Pottery Class
description: Hands-on clay sessions designed for kids aged 5–12. They build, squish, and shape — and walk away with something fired and glazed to take home. Parents welcome to join.

host.name: Min Chen
host.bio: Min has been a ceramics artist and educator for over a decade. She designed the Clay Play curriculum specifically for children aged 5–12, with a focus on sensory exploration over precision. She genuinely believes clay is one of the most honest materials a child can work with.

whatToExpect:
Kids start with a ball of air-dry clay and zero instructions. Min observes what each child naturally gravitates toward before gently guiding them toward a finished piece — usually a small animal, a bowl, or whatever they've decided to make that day.

Parents are welcome to sit alongside and join in. The studio is set up so adults can work on their own piece while keeping an eye on their child.

Finished pieces are left to dry and can be collected 3–5 days later, glazed and ready to take home. Min photographs every piece before collection so you have a record even if it doesn't survive the MRT ride.

title: Laser Tag Singapore – Hosted Team Experience
description: Suited-up, mission-based laser tag for corporate teams, schools, and group events. Four game modes (Domination, Survival, Capture the Flag, Protect the VIP) with facilitators handling briefings, gear, scoring, and flow. Great for getting a big group laughing and actually talking to each other — no combat experience required.

title: Laser Tag Team Building Singapore
description: Channel your inner soldier and go ham in a laser tag battle with your colleagues or kakis. Team Bonding SG runs games at their Stadium MRT battleground, local parks like Fort Canning or Bishan, or even your own venue. Multiple game modes available — classic deathmatch, capture the flag, and more. Great for team building or just a legit excuse to shoot your friends.

title: Learn Sourdough Bread Baking: Beginner-friendly Workshop in Singapore
description: Get your hands floury at this beginner-friendly sourdough workshop held at Leedon Heights. Choose between German-style rye or white sourdough — you'll learn starter care, dough shaping, and baking tips from scratch. You go home with dough you made yourself, ready to bake the next day. Note: the host has left Singapore, so no more in-person classes are available.

title: Learn the Basics of Macramé in our Macramé Wall Hanging Workshop
description: Ever made friendship bands as a kid? Macramé is basically that, grown up. Joette from Knoette walks you through the knotting basics to create your own wall hanging — all materials included. Great if you're craving something slow and hands-on away from the usual Singapore hustle.

title: Leather Crafting Workshop with Hermes Leather
description: Ever wanted to work with the same premium Epsom leather as those fancy Hermès bags? The Leather Society lets you do exactly that — you'll craft your own luxury leather goods while picking up proper techniques from a knowledgeable host. Small group of up to 6 so you actually get attention. Great if you want to make something genuinely nice with your hands.

title: Living Clay Pottery Workshop (Single Session)
description: A cosy home studio run by a husband-and-wife potter duo — sessions are capped at 6 pax so it actually feels intimate. You'll learn hand-building and coiling techniques, plus get a cheeky go on the electric wheel. Your finished piece gets glazed and fired, ready for collection in 2–3 weeks. Great if you need to slow down and make something with your hands.

title: Macrame Bracelet Workshop
description: Learn the basics of macrame and walk away with your own handmade bracelet — all materials included. Choose between black or brown cord, perfect for beginners with zero experience. Book ahead (no walk-ins!), and slots run on weekday afternoons and Saturday mornings. Call to register at least 3 days before.

title: Macramé Plant Hanger Workshop
description: Learn the art of macramé knotting and walk away with your own handmade plant hanger. Hosted by Joette from Knoette, this 3-hour session is a solid way to slow down and get off your phone for a bit. All materials provided, so just show up and start knotting. Great for beginners and plant lovers alike.

title: Make Pasta By Hand & Enjoy Lunch @ The Sundowner
description: Roll up your sleeves and make fresh pasta from scratch at The Sundowner's rooftop nature sanctuary near Bukit Timah. You'll forage for herbs, knead dough, and then actually eat what you made — alfresco style. Great for a chill weekend morning with friends or family. Kids (8+) and pets welcome too.

title: Master the Art of Ramen
description: Learn to make proper Japanese ramen from scratch — fresh noodles, chashu pork, shoyu and miso broths, and those wobbly soft-boiled ramen eggs. It's a solid 4-hour hands-on class that'll have you ditching the instant noodle packets for good. Great if you want to actually impress someone at a dinner party.

title: Mindful Glow: Candlelit Sound Bath Meditation
description: Switch off and lie down in a candlelit room at Fort Canning while Tibetan singing bowls, crystal bowls, and tuning forks do all the work. A trained practitioner leads the session — great whether you've never meditated before or you're a regular. Blankets and pillows provided, just bring yourself and your stress.

title: Modern Brush Pen Calligraphy / Lettering Workshop
description: Pick up a brush pen and learn modern calligraphy from scratch — strokes, letterforms, flourishes and all. Great for stress relief or team bonding, this workshop suits total beginners and seasoned scribblers alike. You'll walk away with actual skills (and maybe some very nice thank-you cards).

title: Hydroponics for Growing Healthy Salad Greens

Grow in Small Spaces using our techniques, ideal for balconies, HDB flats, condominium . title: Neon Brush: Paint & Sip Workshop in the Dark
description: Paint under neon lights in a retro-futuristic black-light setting — drink in one hand, brush in the other. A guided painting workshop where you mix classic and fluorescent paints to create something totally your own. One drink is included, the vibe is immaculate, and yes, you get to bring your glowing masterpiece home.

title: NeuroScope® Breathwork Workshop
description: A 6-hour breathwork session using the NeuroScope® method, run by Movement & Sports Medicine Centre. Great if you've been meaning to actually do something about stress instead of just talking about it. Expect to leave feeling reset — or at least very well-oxygenated.

title: Oil Painting I – VI
description: Learn oil painting from one of Singapore's top arts colleges. This series takes you from the basics of light, composition and brushwork in Level I all the way to more advanced techniques by Level III and beyond. Sessions run every Saturday over 8 weeks — great for beginners and those with some experience alike. SkillsFuture claimable too.

title: Oil Painting Program - Beginner
description: A proper 12-lesson oil painting course for true beginners — no experience needed. You'll work through still life, landscapes, and portraits, finishing with an alla prima portraiture session. Classes are flexible, max 6 pax, and all materials are included. Great if you want to actually learn oil painting, not just dabble.

title: Oil Painting Trial Class
description: Never touched oil paints before? This 2h 15min trial class at Visual Arts Centre eases you in — sketch, blend, and go wet-on-wet with a pro instructor by your side. All materials (canvas, paints, brushes, even aprons) are included, so just show up. Great for total beginners or anyone wanting a low-commitment dip into oil painting.

title: Oil Painting Workshop
description: Learn the classic art of oil painting with SGArtClass — covering everything from blending techniques to tools and materials. Suits both total beginners and those looking to level up. Expect a chill, guided session where you actually walk away with something you made yourself.

title: Paint & Sip
description: Grab a drink and get painting — no skill required. COZE+'s Paint & Sip session gives you 3 hours of free-and-easy art jamming with a canvas, all the acrylic materials you need, and unlimited soft drinks, coffee, and tea included. Perfect for total beginners just looking for a chill creative outlet.

title: Paint & Sip
description: Grab a brush, pour yourself a drink, and get painting with WE ART's Paint & Sip session. A chill, no-pressure way to make something with your hands while enjoying a good time with friends. Great for beginners who just want a fun night out without taking art too seriously.

title: Paint & Sip
description: Grab a brush, pour yourself a drink, and get painting at WE ART's Orchard studio. BYOB (they'll provide the glasses), pick from five styles like impasto or couples painting, and let their instructors guide you through it. No experience needed — just show up, sip, and see what happens on the canvas.

title: Paint-Your-Own Pottery Session
description: Pick a ceramic piece, paint it your way, and let the studio handle the glazing and firing. Open to all ages and skill levels, so no experience needed — just show up and have fun. Based in a cosy studio at Coronation Plaza, it's a solid activity for families, dates, or a chill afternoon out. Collect your finished piece in 4–6 weeks.

title: Pasta By Hand
description: Skip the jarred stuff — learn to make real pasta from scratch using just eggs and flour. You'll knead dough, run it through a pasta machine, and shape either pappardelle or ravioli before sitting down to eat what you made (with Prosecco, no less). There's even a rooftop herb forage in the mix. Weekends only for join-in sessions; private bookings flexible.
location: Sundowner SG (rooftop — check with provider for exact area)

title: Pasta Making Class Singapore
description: Learn to make fresh pasta from scratch — knead, roll, cut, and fill your way through varieties like Ravioli and Tagliatelle under a pro chef's guidance. You'll pick up proper al dente technique and get to eat what you make. Great for beginners who want real kitchen skills, not just a recipe printout.

title: Pasta Masterclass by Fiamma
description: Learn to make handmade pasta from scratch with Executive Sous Chef Antonio Corsaro at Capella Singapore's intimate Chef's Table. Sessions rotate between Angel Hair and Tagliatelle, held on the last Sunday of each month. At $60++ a pop, it's a proper hands-on class — not just a demo. Recommended for 16 and above.

title: Private Pasta Making & Lunch
description: Make fresh pasta from scratch in a private session at the Old Bukit Timah Fire Station — yes, you even forage for herbs. Think squid ink pasta, good vibes, and a nature backdrop. Great for birthdays or hens parties where you want something more memorable than just drinks. Hosts Clarence and Candice make it genuinely fun, not just a cooking demo.

title: Private Wine Tasting Experience
description: Bring the sommelier to you — Chef De Maison runs private wine tasting events at your home or office, covering French, Italian, and Spanish wines. Learn how to taste, serve, and pair wine with food, all guided by experienced sommeliers. Events are fully customised to your vibe, whether it's a chill home session or a corporate wine & cheese night.

title: Professional Chinese Calligraphy & Ink Painting Course
description: Learn Chinese calligraphy and ink painting from a master artist in a bilingual (English & Mandarin) setting — so don't worry if your Mandarin is rusty. Each session splits time between brushwork calligraphy and expressive ink painting on rice paper. All materials provided, and you walk away with a piece you actually made yourself.

title: Professional Oil Painting Art Course
description: Learn oil painting from scratch or level up your existing skills at Visual Arts Centre's studio near Dhoby Ghaut. Classes cover still life, landscapes, portraiture, and more — taught by professionally trained artists using an academy-school approach. All materials included, so just show up and paint. Suitable for teens and adults, beginners to advanced.

title: Professional Watercolour Painting Art Course
description: Pick up watercolour painting at your own pace in a proper studio setting — no experience needed. You'll cover everything from still life and landscapes to portraits and figure drawing, guided by a professional instructor. Materials are all provided, and you'll walk away with a completed artwork each 1–3 sessions. Good for teens, working adults, and retirees alike.

title: Resin Art Experience
description: Learn resin art from scratch in this 2-session course at NAFA. You'll explore acrylic pour techniques, play with colourants and tools, and walk away with your own abstract resin pieces. Trainer Cindy Neo (founder of Room to Imagine) keeps it hands-on and beginner-friendly. Note: materials not included in the course fee.

title: Resin Art Workshop
description: Get your hands sticky with epoxy resin and walk away with your own coaster, keychain, pendant, or tray. SGArtClass guides you through the whole process — mixing, pouring, and curing — so no experience needed. Good for team bonding or just a chill creative afternoon. Customisable themes available too.

title: Salsa Classes in Singapore
provider: Actfa School of Dance & Performing Arts
description: Learn Salsa at ACTFA — whether you're a total newbie or looking to level up your footwork. They cover On1, On2, Cuban Style, Rueda, and even Styling classes, so there's something for every level. No partner needed; they rotate in class. Multiple locations across Singapore with flexible pricing packages.
location: Little India / Bukit Panjang / Bukit Merah

title: Salsa Cubana Beginner 1A Course (Partnerwork)
description: New to salsa? This beginner course at Bugis teaches you Cuban salsa from scratch — proper technique, lead/follow roles, and enough moves to actually dance at a social. No partner needed, classes rotate. 4 sessions of 1.5hrs each, or drop in for a single trial first.

title: Screen Printing Workshop with STPI
description: Get hands-on with screen printing at this workshop run by STPI, one of Singapore's most respected print and paper art studios. Part of the Light to Night festival programme, it's a solid pick if you've always been curious about printmaking but never got around to trying it. Expect to walk away with something you actually made yourself.

title: Screen Printing Workshop with STPI
description: Ever wondered how screenprinting actually works? This 2.5-hour workshop at National Gallery lets you make your own editioned prints, inspired by the Kim Lim retrospective. Choose between a parent-child co-creation session or an open adult session — both led by STPI's lead instructor. Materials and exhibition entry included.

title: Signature Singapore Bike Tour
description: A 4-hour guided bike tour hitting all of Singapore's greatest hits — Marina Bay, Chinatown, Haji Lane, Little India, Kampong Glam and more. You'll get a knowledgeable English-speaking guide, bike rental, and refreshments included. Great for families or first-timers who want to actually see the city instead of just Grab-ing everywhere.

title: Signature Tumbler Painting Workshop
description: Singapore's first tumbler painting studio lets you pick stencils, grab a premium stainless steel tumbler, and go to town with guided instruction — no art skills needed. In 2 hours you'll walk out with a personalised, durable tumbler you'll actually use daily. Great for dates, families, tourists, or just a chill creative afternoon near Jalan Besar.

title: Singapore Axe Factor Axe Throwing Experience
description: Chuck axes at targets and unleash your inner lumberjack — no experience needed. Singapore Axe Factor is one of the few spots in SG where you can do proper axe throwing, great for blowing off steam or impressing your friends. Fun for groups, birthday parties, or just a random Tuesday.

title: Singapore: Axe Factor (Axe Throwing Experience)
description: Ever wanted to hurl an axe at something? Now you can — legally. Axe Factor lets you throw hatchets at a target board 14 feet away, with safety briefing and coaching included. Great for stress relief, friendly competition, or just doing something completely different. Solo or with a group, it slaps.

title: Singapore Hawker Favorites Cooking Class
description: Learn to cook legit Singapore hawker classics — think Chilli Crab, Hainanese Chicken Rice, Hokkien Mee and more. Hands-on class where you get the real tricks behind the dishes you've been eating at hawker centres your whole life. Great for tourists or locals who finally want to know how it's done.

title: Singapore: Light to Night Bike Tour
description: Cycle through Kampong Glam, Little India, Chinatown, and Marina Bay with a local guide as the city shifts from day to night. Small group of up to 8, so it's actually personal — not a cattle herd on wheels. Bike, helmet, snack, and souvenir included. Best done at night when the heat is slightly more survivable.

title: Professional Oil Painting Trial Art Class | Art Course | Art Lesson (Suitable for beginners I All art materials provided)
description: Wine, brushes, and zero judgment. A casual guided painting session where the vibe matters more than the art. Great for solo evenings or small groups.

host.name: Visual Arts Centre Singapore
host.bio: Canvas & Co. was founded by two art school graduates who wanted to make painting social rather than precious. They've hosted over 1,000 sessions and have a strict no-judgment policy that they take very seriously.

whatToExpect:
You'll arrive to find your canvas set up with a light pencil sketch guide and your first glass of wine poured. The session is guided — a Canvas & Co. artist walks through the painting step by step — but the pace is loose and the music is good.

The subject changes each session: landscapes, botanicals, abstract colour fields. You won't know the exact painting until you arrive, which keeps regulars coming back.

Everyone leaves with a finished (or at least complete) piece. Canvas & Co. provides all materials — brushes, acrylics, canvas, aprons. Just bring yourself and a willingness to ruin a shirt.

title: Sip 'N' Paint with Live Demonstration & Step-by-Step Guide | Art Jamming (Fully Guided) | BYOB!
description: Bring your own wine, beer, or bubble tea and spend 3 hours painting something you actually like — guided step-by-step by an art instructor. No experience needed, all materials provided. Great for a chill date night or a group hangout at a studio in Geylang, near MRT.

title: Sound Bath Classes
description: Lie back and let the sounds wash over you — singing bowls, crystal bowls, Koshi bells, ocean drums and more. These sound bath sessions at Grounded Spaces are designed to ease you into deep relaxation and meditation. Great if your mind won't shut up and you need something to actually help you unwind.

title: Sound Bath Singapore
description: Lie down, close your eyes, and let waves of singing bowls, gongs, and chimes wash over you. Unika Yoga's Sound Bath sessions are small and personal — no experience needed, just show up in comfy clothes. Great for when your brain won't shut up and your body is begging for a proper rest.

title: Stand-Up Comedy Workshop - Level 1 Intro to Stand-Up
provider: Mad About Comedy / Comedy Hub Singapore
description: Ever wondered if you're actually funny? This 2-hour intro workshop by comedian Scott Mitchell covers joke writing, stage presence, and mic technique — no experience needed. You'll even get a chance to watch live open mic acts right after. Guaranteed performance slot at a future show if you're keen (no pressure though).

title: TactSim Indoor PVP Airsoft
description: Singapore's first indoor PvP airsoft arena, where movable wall panels keep things fresh every season. Go head-to-head in Capture the Flag or King of the Hill, or test your aim at the target shooting range. All gear provided — just bring your competitive streak and covered shoes. Must be 18+ to play.

title: Terrarium Making
description: Build your own little world in a glass jar. No prior experience needed — just a love for plants and a willingness to get your hands dirty. Perfect for unwinding after a long week.

host.name: The Green Fingers Team
host.bio: The Green Fingers Studio team are plant obsessives who left corporate jobs to spend their days surrounded by moss and succulents. They've taught over 3,000 people to build terrariums and still get excited when someone makes their first one.

whatToExpect:
You'll choose your vessel from a selection of glass containers — open bowls, closed ecosystems, geometric shapes — and then your plants from the studio's resident collection of ferns, moss, succulents, and air plants.

The team guides you through layering: drainage gravel, activated charcoal, soil mix, then planting. The process takes about 90 minutes if you're decisive, longer if you're the type who rearranges things eight times.

You'll leave with a fully assembled terrarium and a care card specific to your plant selection. Terrariums that are well-matched to their environment can last for years with minimal attention.

title: The Art of Cocktail Mixology Class
description: Skip the bar tab and learn to mix your own cocktails and mocktails at home. You'll cover the basics of spirits, bar tools, glassware, and how to make classics like Mojito, Old Fashioned, and Whiskey Sour — plus mocktail options. Taught by experienced mixologists in a hands-on setting. Great for parties, date nights, or just levelling up your hosting game.

title: The Paddle Lodge at MacRitchie Reservoir
description: Rent a kayak and head out on MacRitchie Reservoir — one of Singapore's most scenic spots. Choose from single or double sit-on-top kayaks, closed deck recreational kayaks, or even racing K1/K2 canoes if you're feeling sporty. Great way to escape the city without actually leaving it.

title: The Ultimate Calligraphy Course
description: A proper 5-week calligraphy course that takes you from zero to flourishing — literally. Leah breaks down the theory, strokes, and design logic behind beautiful lettering so you're not just copying blindly. Great for beginners who've tried YouTube and gave up, or practitioners who know something's off but can't figure out what. Held in Central Singapore.

title: Watercolour Painting Workshop with Chankerk – Complete Guidance for Serious Learners
description: Want to actually get good at watercolour — not just dabble? This workshop by professional artist Chankerk is built for people who mean business, whether you're a total beginner or an amateur looking to sharpen your skills. Expect proper eye-mind-hand guidance and a focus on getting those luminous, rich colours right.

title: Watercolour Painting Workshop
description: Pick up watercolour basics (or level up your skills) in a chill, guided workshop that's equal parts art class and therapy session. You'll learn wet-in-wet, dry brush, colour theory, and even some fun tricks like salt textures. Works for total beginners, seasoned painters, and corporate team bonding alike.

title: WSQ Prepare and Serve Cocktails (2 Day In-Person)
description: Learn to make classic cocktails like Mojitos, Old Fashioneds and Margaritas in this 2-day WSQ-accredited hands-on course. You'll cover spirits theory, bar techniques, glassware, and even food pairing — plus sit a written and practical assessment. SkillsFuture credits and SSG funding applicable, so it's a solid deal for anyone serious about bartending.
